lab.design_status: predeclared research design choices; not 2026 FullHouse settings (see paper/FHR3B_SCOPE.md)
lab.horizon_status: initial research horizon; not assumed sufficient

notes: Tournament repetitions are stochastic reruns CONDITIONAL on one frozen field per constructed regime (spread, crowded_cutoff, style_diverse). They are not independent replications of a field regime: no regime-level inference, and no universal claims (e.g. 'crowded fields require X rounds').

mu_field = long-run expected performance against random partitions of the controlled field under the specified match semantics; mu_swiss = long-run expected outcome under the specified adaptive Swiss mechanism. Both are finite-sample ESTIMATES, neither is universal poker skill or an oracle ranking; they can disagree because multiplayer, non-transitive games need not admit one context-free ranking.
Accuracy against mu_swiss measures convergence / repeatability / finite-sample approximation to the Swiss mechanism, not independent normative fairness.

Identity error (changed qualifiers, top-6 overlap) and strength error (qualification regret, boundary strength loss; BB per ordinary-equivalent match) are reported together. '*_ref_propagated' intervals add reference uncertainty (joint reference bootstrap); 'reference_self_regret' is the regret floor due to reference uncertainty alone; 'clear_*' counts ignore swaps inside the reference-ambiguous set.
Experiment B holds the SCHEDULED (maximum) hand budget fixed, not actual simulator compute.

Experiment C compares adaptive Swiss with exogenous replay of schedules generated by the adaptive process (fresh poker randomness); a targeted counterfactual comparison, not a complete causal decomposition.
Experiment D compares operational evaluation packages (duplicate arms also change rounds or match length); not the isolated effect of turning duplicate play on.

pairing.baseline: independent across fields and modes (different fields/games); shared seed family
pairing.budget_sweep: paired by replicate index: shared tournament seeds, identical round-1 tables and a shared hand-prefix of round-1 chance; tables diverge after round 1
pairing.duplicate_play: paired by replicate index: shared tournament seeds (round-1 tables); work is reported as scheduled and actually played hands, never assumed equal
pairing.frozen_schedule: paired by replicate: frozen replicate r replays the complete table schedule of baseline tournament r with fresh cards/decisions (same round-1 tables); replicates are independent
pairing.round_sweep: paired: checkpoint leaderboards are exact round prefixes of the same horizon tournaments
pairing.schedule_diagnostic: paired by (source, replay): frozen and adaptive replay j share card/decision seeds and round-1 tables; sources are independent
pairing.swiss_reference: separate namespace from every finite-budget cell
